name: NIST SSDF
full_name: NIST Special Publication 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1: Recommendations for Mitigating the Risk of Software Vulnerabilities
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)

sources.title: NIST SP 800-218, SSDF Version 1.1 practices table (spreadsheet)
NIST SP 800-218, Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1

control_flags.formerly: The identifier a task had before version 1.1 moved it, where the table notes one.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable tasks that are performed, with a partially performed task counting as half. The SSDF defines no score or maturity levels; this index is an HCG measure of progress.

rules.summary: The SSDF describes outcomes and does not prescribe how each practice is implemented, so a task is assessed on whether its outcome is reached.
rules.quote: The SSDF does not prescribe how to implement each practice.

rules.summary: Not every practice applies to every use case; the organization decides by risk which practices are relevant, so a task can be not applicable.
rules.quote: Not all practices are applicable to all use cases; organizations should adopt a risk-based approach to determine what practices are relevant, appropriate, and effective to mitigate the threats to their software development practices.

rules.summary: In the implementation index a partially performed task counts as half. This is an HCG convention: the SSDF itself defines no score.
rules.quote: The focus is on the outcomes of the practices rather than on the tools, techniques, and mechanisms to do so.

glossary.definition: The NIST Secure Software Development Framework, a set of secure software development practices arranged by practice group, practice and task.
Software development life cycle: the process of designing, building, testing, releasing and maintaining software.
An example NIST gives of a tool, process or method that could help perform a task; examples are illustrative, not required.
National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. agency that publishes the SSDF.
